predecessors.name: Qasimid State
predecessors.text: the Qasimid state, 'also known as the Imamate of Yemen' (Qasimid state page), which lost its coastal possessions to the Wahhabis after 1803

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Sana'a and the highlands: the Ottomans took 'San'a and making it the capital of the Yemen Vilayet in 1872' and conquered the northern highlands by 1873

ledger.x: 1814: Cliopatria restarts the Zaydi imamate of Sana'a.
1872: the Ottomans take Sana'a and make it the capital of the Yemen Vilayet.

wars.name: Wahhabi conquest of the Zaydi coast
wars.outcome: The Wahhabi movement cost the Zaidi state its coast after 1803; the imam regained it temporarily in 1818.

wars.name: Egyptian intervention in the Tihama
wars.outcome: The Egyptian viceroy of the Ottoman Sultan wrested the coast from the ruler in Sana'a.

wars.name: Ottoman reconquest of Yemen
wars.outcome: The Ottomans returned to the Tihama in 1849 and took Sana'a in 1872, making it the capital of the Yemen Vilayet; the northern highlands were conquered by 1873 and the Zaydi imams kept Upper Yemen under formal recognition.

certainty.note: Highland tribal frontiers (Hashid and Bakil) and an unsurveyed coast; no page gives a boundary.
